What is the immediate physical cargo of bulk nuclear mRNA export?
A translating polysome inside the nucleus
An mRNA associates with proteins that influence export and passage. DNA remains nuclear, ordinary cytoplasmic polysomes are not the export cargo, and extracellular vesicles are unrelated.
Which protein pair is the principal receptor for bulk mammalian cellular mRNA export?
NXF1–NXT1 mediates major mRNA export. Ran regulators maintain a nucleotide-state asymmetry, UPF1 and SMG1 act in NMD, and U1/U2 participate in splicing.
Which association best connects a typical 5′ cap with nuclear mRNP formation?
The nuclear cap-binding complex contains CBP20 and CBP80. The synthetase charges tRNA, DNA polymerase replicates DNA, and XRN1 degrades accessible RNA from its 5′ end.
Which feature of FG nucleoporins is most relevant to RNA export?
FG repeat regions participate in selective receptor-mediated passage; the other activities do not describe their transport function.
Which factor chiefly promotes nuclear mRNP assembly in the TREX model?
UAP56 participates in nuclear assembly; DDX19 remodels export cargo at release, RanGAP promotes Ran hydrolysis, and eRF1 recognizes termination codons during translation.
What is the main role of DDX19/Dbp5 in bulk mRNA export?
Cytoplasmic-face remodeling of an emerging mRNP
Addition of amino acids to tRNA
DDX19/Dbp5 helps remove export-associated factors and release cargo. Poly(A) polymerase, RNA polymerase III and aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases have the other roles.
Which molecule is a known regulator of the DDX19/Dbp5 release machinery?
Tubulin as an obligatory export receptor
Gle1, with IP6 in the canonical system, regulates the ATPase. Ligase, telomerase RNA and tubulin are not its corresponding core regulatory partners.
Which statement correctly distinguishes bulk NXF1-mediated export from an exportin route?
NXF1 directly requires nuclear RanGTP for every cargo-binding event
Bulk mRNA release uses ATP-dependent remodeling; many exportins use RanGTP
Both routes require a lipid-soluble RNA

The key difference is the direct source of directionality. Cellular energy is required, but NXF1 is not a classical Ran-dependent exportin, and RNA passes through pores rather than dissolving in membrane lipid.
Where does RCC1 primarily promote nucleotide exchange on Ran?
RCC1 is a nuclear Ran guanine-nucleotide exchange factor. Cytoplasmic RanGAP promotes hydrolysis rather than exchange.
Why is cytoplasmic RanGTP hydrolysis important for exportin-mediated transport?
It directly adds a cap to the RNA
It facilitates disassembly of the export complex
Hydrolysis changes Ran's nucleotide state and favors cargo release and receptor recycling. The other reactions are not functions of Ran.
Which receptor directly recognizes appropriate folded tRNA in a RanGTP-dependent model?
Exportin-t is a tRNA exporter. Pol II transcribes other RNA classes, UPF2 participates in NMD, and XRN1 is a nuclease.
Which statement about tRNA export is most accurate?
Every tRNA is fully modified and spliced before leaving every nucleus
The anticodon alone determines all export
Some tRNAs undergo further maturation after nuclear export
tRNA is exported only when attached to a translating ribosome

Maturation itineraries vary, including cytoplasmic splicing of some budding-yeast tRNAs. Anticodon identity alone does not define export competence, and a translating ribosome is not required for nuclear export.
Which adaptor is a representative component of large ribosomal subunit export?
Nmd3 helps recruit CRM1 to pre-60S particles. U1 acts in splicing, cap-binding protein alone is not the specified adaptor, and primase makes primers for DNA replication.
What is the typical final destination of a spliceosomal snRNP?
Splicing of nuclear pre-mRNA takes place in the nucleus. Some snRNA precursors visit the cytoplasm for assembly but subsequently return.
A zipcode in an RNA most directly specifies what?
A protein's amino acid sequence in all cases
A contribution to the RNA's spatial localization
The replication origin of the chromosome
A localization element recruits or influences localization machinery; a 3′ UTR zipcode can act without altering the coding sequence.
Which RNA localization mechanism does not require a motor to carry each RNA to its destination?
Diffusive arrival and local capture can establish enrichment. The other alternatives explicitly involve cytoskeletal motors.
Why can a localized RNA remain translationally repressed during movement?
To prevent inappropriate protein production before arrival
Because all cytoplasmic RNA lacks ribosomes
Because it has permanently lost its coding sequence
Because nuclear pores destroy all caps
Repression can restrict protein synthesis to the destination. It is regulated and need not reflect damage or a lack of translation machinery.
Which observation is consistent with normal nuclear retention rather than necessarily a defect?
A functional nucleolar RNA concentrated in the nucleolus
Every mature enzyme mRNA trapped in the nucleus
A normal tRNA never reaching its required cytoplasmic pool
A reporter losing export after receptor depletion
Nucleolar RNAs may function at their nuclear location. The other observations suggest possible defects in delivery of normally exported cargo.
What is the nuclear RNA exosome?
A membrane-bound extracellular particle in this context
The RNA exosome is a multiprotein complex with associated nuclease functions. It is not an extracellular vesicle.
Which event is central to canonical mammalian nonsense-mediated decay?
Translation termination in an NMD-promoting context
NMD is triggered through translation-associated recognition, not simply by the presence of a mutation or the act of export.
Where is an exon junction complex typically deposited relative to a newly formed junction?
At the poly(A) tail in all transcripts
Typical deposition is 20–24 nt upstream of many splice junctions. The 50–55 nt figure refers to a commonly used stop-to-junction NMD predictor.
Which protein is central to NMD?
UPF1 is an ATP-dependent RNA helicase involved in NMD. The other components function in different transport or replication systems.
What does removal of a 5′ cap commonly facilitate during cytoplasmic RNA turnover?
Decapping generates an accessible 5′ end for enzymes such as XRN1. It is not a splicing, replication or Ran exchange reaction.
Why is total cellular RNA abundance insufficient to identify an export defect?
Export redistributes RNA and decay can also change abundance
Every RNA is always found equally in both compartments
RNA abundance can never be measured
Total abundance conflates synthesis and destruction and does not reveal distribution. Export can alter distribution with or without a change in total counts.
Which method directly provides spatial information about a selected RNA in fixed cells?
Western blot of whole-cell protein alone
RNA FISH uses complementary probes to reveal location. The other methods do not identify the spatial distribution of a specific RNA.
Assertion: A normal intronless mRNA can be exported. Reason: Export competence can arise through processing and RNA–protein associations other than splice-deposited EJC.
Both true; reason does not explain assertion
The absence of an intron is not a maturation defect; alternative recruitment routes explain why a splice-dependent mark is not universally essential.
Assertion: Bulk mRNA export is generally Ran-independent at its direct receptor step. Reason: All eukaryotic nuclear transport processes are unaffected by changes in Ran.
Both true; reason does not explain assertion
NXF1-dependent export differs from Ran-dependent exportins. Global Ran perturbation can still affect many transport and gene-expression processes.
Assertion: A nuclear exosome defect can increase nuclear RNA abundance. Reason: Slower removal can enlarge a nuclear pool even if synthesis is unchanged.
Both true; reason does not explain assertion
The balance of production and loss determines abundance. Reduced degradation can increase RNA without changing transcription or export.
Assertion: NMD usually acts only before a message has encountered a ribosome. Reason: Recognition of abnormal termination in the canonical pathway requires translation.
Both true; reason does not explain assertion
Canonical NMD is translation dependent, which contradicts the assertion.

Assertion: Loss of a 3′ UTR zipcode can alter local protein production without changing the encoded amino acid sequence. Reason: A UTR can specify RNA localization while remaining outside the coding sequence.
Both true; reason does not explain assertion
A noncoding regulatory element can control spatial translation; alteration of the element does not necessarily alter the polypeptide's primary sequence.

Which statements are correct? I. NXF1 and NXT1 form a receptor pair. II. UAP56 contributes to mRNP assembly. III. DDX19 supplies the canonical tRNA exportin receptor. IV. FG repeats interact with transport receptors.
I, II and IV describe bulk export. DDX19 remodels mRNPs and is not the tRNA receptor.
Which statements correctly describe Ran? I. RCC1 favors nuclear nucleotide exchange. II. RanGAP promotes cytoplasmic hydrolysis. III. RanGTP always causes cargo release from every transport receptor.
I and II establish asymmetry. III is false because exportins commonly assemble cargo complexes with RanGTP, whereas many importins release cargo in response to it.
Match A. NXF1–NXT1; B. Exportin-t; C. Nmd3; D. ZBP1 with 1. tRNA transport; 2. beta-actin zipcode recognition; 3. bulk mRNA export; 4. pre-60S export adaptor.
NXF1–NXT1 serves bulk mRNA, exportin-t serves tRNA, Nmd3 links pre-60S to export machinery, and ZBP1 recognizes the actin localization element.
Match A. RNA FISH; B. Pulse-chase; C. Reporter zipcode deletion; D. UPF1 depletion with 1. RNA movement over time; 2. test NMD dependence; 3. spatial localization; 4. test element necessity.
FISH maps RNA, pulse-chase follows labeled molecules, deletion tests necessity, and UPF1 perturbation can test NMD involvement.
Select the correct statements. I. Nuclear retention and decay are distinct. II. Every nuclear RNA is defective. III. Normal RNAs can eventually undergo regulated decay. IV. NMD repairs mutant DNA.
Retention does not necessarily destroy RNA, and normal turnover occurs. Nuclear RNAs can be functional; NMD changes RNA abundance rather than repairing DNA.
An export-competent pool has s=60 molecules/min, k_e=0.2/min and k_n=0.1/min. What is N at steady state?
N=s/(k_e+k_n)=60/0.3=200 molecules. Dividing by export alone ignores nuclear loss; adding rates in the numerator is dimensionally wrong.
For N=200 molecules, k_e=0.2/min and k_c=0.05/min, find the steady-state cytoplasmic count.
Export flux is 40 molecules/min. At steady state C=40/0.05=800. The value 40 is a flux, not a count.
Two cells each have C/N=2. Cell A has k_c=0.10/min; cell B has k_c=0.04/min. Under the model, which export rate is correct?
C/N=k_e/k_c, so k_e=2k_c. An identical ratio does not imply identical rates if cytoplasmic decay differs.
A nuclear molecule faces k_e=0.15/min and k_n=0.05/min as competing first-order hazards. What fraction is expected to export eventually?
The export probability is 0.15/(0.15+0.05)=0.75. The remaining quarter is expected to undergo nuclear decay.
An isolated cytoplasmic RNA pool has no new influx and k_c=0.10/min. Its approximate half-life is:
t_1/2=ln(2)/0.10=6.93 min. The reciprocal rate of 10 min is the mean lifetime for this model, not its half-life.
The last exon junction is at nucleotide 500. Two mammalian reporter stop positions are 420 and 480 under otherwise matched conditions. Which prediction is most appropriate?
420 more likely NMD by the classic junction rule
480 more likely because it is closer to the junction
Both must be degraded in every cell
The stop-to-junction separations are approximately 80 and 20 nt. The first supports a retained downstream EJC; the second is below the usual 50–55 nt threshold. These are probabilistic predictions.
At steady state s=40 molecules/min, k_e=0.1/min, k_n=0 and k_c=0.05/min. If k_e halves and a new steady state is reached, what changes?
With no nuclear decay, N=s/k_e rises from 400 to 800. Export flux equals s at both steady states, so C=s/k_c=800. The transient behavior can differ.

After a pulse, 120 labeled nuclear molecules exist. Later, 35 nuclear and 65 cytoplasmic labeled molecules are detected. What fraction has disappeared from the measured pools, assuming complete recovery of intact labels and no new labeled molecules?
120−(35+65)=20 molecules, and 20/120≈16.7%. The fall in nuclear count alone overestimates loss because export transfers intact molecules.
A mutant has normal nascent RNA, fully spliced nuclear RNA, reduced NXF1 association with cargo and lower cytoplasmic RNA. Which is the strongest proximal hypothesis?
Loss of a cytoplasmic zipcode only
Normal synthesis and splicing plus reduced receptor loading support an assembly defect. The other choices do not explain the reduced cargo–receptor association.
A mutant mRNA binds NXF1 normally but the receptor's FG-binding surface is impaired. Which result would support the hypothesized defect?
Normal receptor loading with reduced pore passage
Loss of exon junctions from DNA
Receptor loading is intact, but engagement with the selective barrier is impaired. This separates cargo recognition from translocation.
Depletion of DDX19 causes pore-associated mRNPs and reduced released cytoplasmic RNA. Which rescue comparison best tests the proposed role?
Wild-type DDX19 versus an expressed ATPase-defective variant
A different promoter versus no promoter
Wild-type tRNA versus mutant DNA ligase
Two unrelated fluorescence colors without perturbation
A matched functional-versus-catalytic mutant rescue tests whether ATPase-dependent release is required. Expression and localization of both variants must be checked.
An RNA FISH image shows high nuclear oligo(dT) signal after a treatment. Which additional result most specifically supports redistribution of mature mRNA?
Gene-specific mature RNA counts rise in nucleus and fall in cytoplasm while early synthesis is similar
Compartment counts of mature RNA with synthesis controls support an export phenotype. Oligo(dT) alone can be influenced by tail length and RNA composition.
A splice donor mutant has little cytoplasmic reporter RNA. Nuclear exosome inhibition causes strong accumulation of unspliced nuclear reporter but does not restore cytoplasmic RNA. What follows?
Nuclear decay removed some retained RNA, but its inhibition did not restore export competence
NMD was proven to act in the nucleus before translation
The mutation must be repaired at the DNA level
Exosome inhibition restores all RNA functions
The two measurements separate nuclear destruction from export. Accumulation after nuclease inhibition does not establish successful maturation or delivery.

In a matched reporter pair, deleting a 3′ UTR element abolishes peripheral enrichment but total RNA remains unchanged. Adding the element to a diffuse reporter induces enrichment. What does this support?
The element contributes to localization and is sufficient in the tested reporter context
The element changes the protein sequence necessarily
The element is a universal export receptor
The element acts independently of all proteins
Deletion supports necessity in the original context, and addition supports sufficiency in the reporter context. Neither proves universal independence from cellular machinery.
Live tracking shows RNA arrives at the cell edge at the same rate in mutant and wild type, but mutant particles leave the edge sooner. Which step is most directly implicated?
Normal arrival with shortened residence points to retention at the destination, not necessarily impaired directed transport or nuclear export.
A motor inhibitor reduces RNA enrichment at the cell edge but also changes cell shape. What is the best interpretation?
The result is compatible with motor dependence but indirect effects must be controlled
The RNA must be degraded by NMD
No RNA can be localized by diffusion
A perturbation of cytoskeletal motors can alter the geometry and anchors as well as transport. Track movement and control cell organization before making a strong causal claim.
After RCC1 impairment, tRNA export declines. Bulk mRNA export also declines later. Which conclusion is justified?
Ran may directly affect tRNA export and indirectly disturb mRNA export machinery
NXF1 must directly bind RanGTP in every mRNA cycle
All RNA export mechanisms are identical
A global Ran perturbation affects many nuclear import and export processes. Later effects on NXF1-dependent transport do not establish direct Ran dependence.
A reporter with an early stop has normal early nuclear production, reduced cytoplasmic abundance and increased stability following UPF1 depletion. Which hypothesis is strengthened?
Translation-dependent NMD contributes to the loss
The nuclear pore no longer exists
The early stop and dependence on a core NMD factor support accelerated surveillance after delivery. Translation dependence and appropriate rescue controls can further strengthen this inference.
A pre-60S export adaptor mutant leaves cytoplasmic mRNA abundance unchanged but lowers protein output. Which other observation fits?
Accumulation of immature large-subunit particles in the nucleus
Universal loss of the 5′ cap from all mRNAs
A lower DNA copy number as the obligatory cause
Every RNA zipcode becomes a stop codon
Ribosomal subunit availability limits translation even if mRNA delivery works. The other alternatives do not follow from a large-subunit export defect.
A normally nuclear lncRNA becomes cytoplasmic after deletion of a retention element but total RNA abundance is unchanged. What is the most defensible consequence?
Its nuclear function may be impaired because localization changed
Its total abundance proves its function is intact
Its genomic DNA has been exported
Spatial misplacement can impair a nuclear role without changing total counts. Cytoplasmic localization alone does not imply protein coding or DNA movement.
